12.36: Man, you have been a citizen in this great state, the world; what difference does it make to you whether it was for five years or three? For what is in keeping with the laws is just for all. Where, then, is the hardship, if it is no tyrant, nor yet an unjust judge, who sends you away from the state, but nature, who brought you into it? It is the same as if a praetor who has hired an actor dismisses him from the stage.—“But I have not finished the five acts, only three of them.”—You are right, but in life three acts are the whole drama; for what makes a complete drama is decided by the one who was once the cause of its making, and now of its undoing: but you are the cause of neither. Depart, then, content, for the one who releases you is content too.
